_readme: TWO MINDS, FOR A LONG CHEAP RUN. One grok, one kimi, and nobody else.
COST: about 14 pence an hour. Kimi is free (your own tinybox) and the grok
seat is the non-reasoning one — measured at $0.79 per 1000 decisions and
0.8 s to answer, the cheapest and fastest thing on any of the three
vendors. At a 20 s cadence that is ~180 calls an hour, so this can run all
day for the price of a coffee.
NO SCRIPTED CONTROL IN THIS ONE, on purpose. Iseabail is normally the most
valuable seat on the board — but a third body in a TWO-mind conversation is
noise, and what is being watched here is whether two minds talk to each
other and trade. Put her back for any run where the question is 'was that
the model or the world'.
THE CHARACTERS ARE CHOSEN TO COLLIDE. One hoards and prices everything; the
other is blunt and asks for what it wants. Six verbs shipped yesterday —
give, offer, accept, attack, and a loose quarry match — and NOT ONE has
ever been used by a real model. This roster is the smallest, cheapest world
in which any of them could possibly happen.
What to look for on the board: the `gold` column moving, a `deeds` line
reading 'I traded ...', and an `offer` in the chat column. If a whole
evening passes with none of those, the session report will say so in its
'what nobody ever did' section — which is a real finding, not a failure.

players.name: Eachann
players.character: You hoard. What you pick up is yours and you do not hand it over for nothing — but you will name a price for anything, and you drive a hard bargain. Gold interests you more than company.

players.name: Coinneach
players.character: You are blunt and you ask for what you need rather than going without. You would rather owe somebody than starve, and you say plainly what you think a thing is worth.
